title: Vector-Network rank-1 atoms with a factorized persistent task coefficient code
hypothesis: A compact task-coordinate factorization of coefficients over shared rank-1 atoms preserves per-input sparse local inference on heldout task compositions while reducing complete bytes versus independent task coefficient tables.
physical_object: K=8 shared rank-1 weight atoms u_k v_k^T
mirror_coordinate: task factors (a,b) selecting coefficients c0 + a*c1 + b*c2 over the atom bank
local_inference: for every input, score atoms by |v_k^T x| and select top-2 before composing output; selection is recomputed per example

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after exact native coefficient-factorization alias or frozen gate miss.

controls: independent per-task coefficient tables over the same atoms
shared coefficient vector without task codes
native low-rank factorization of the task-by-atom coefficient matrix

paid: coefficient bases or full task coefficients

pass_gate: Heldout nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer complete bytes than independent coefficients, average active atoms=2 with changing per-input selections, and strict frontier gain over native low-rank factorization.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific value on exact native low-rank alias, quality miss, savings below 25%, or no strict control frontier gain.

compute.active_MAC_proxy: K input projections plus top-2 rank-1 projections/scales/readout
compute.wall_time: small CPU local-inference loop; not throughput evidence

boundaries: Synthetic linear compositional task maps only; no reproduction of trained Vector Networks or their learning/inference algorithm.
Task factor coordinates are known and charged; no task inference claim.
The per-input atom selection is implemented and audited, but coefficient bases are oracle generated from an additive rank-2 teacher; it is not learned by gradient descent.
Native coefficient factorization is a required direct attribution control.
